steps.description:
Write a program that calls a function that takes in the screen and pen as arguments and perform the following: 1. Draw a horizontal line and a vertical line across the center of the screen. 2. Draw a circle with radius 120 pixels. The center of the circle should be at the intersection of the lines, that is, at (0,0).

Set your turtle speed to 0 as this may take a while to be drawn.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

A grid helps us to see where we draw our shapes.

Write a program that calls a function draw_grid(screen, pen) which takes in the screen and pen as arguments. The function will do the following: 1. Determine the width and height of the screen. 1. Draw lines at 35 pixel intervals away from the center lines so that they form a grid using colour "LightGray". 2. Draw a horizontal line and a vertical line across the center of the screen using colour "gray".

Set your turtle speed to 0 as this may take a while to be drawn.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Create a function draw_circle(pen, radius, x, y) that takes in the radius of a circle in pixels and the position of its center (x, y) in the screen coordinate. It will draw the circle using pen with "black" outline and filled with "yellow".

Write a program that does the following: 1. Call the draw_grid(screen, pen) function implemented in previous exercise to draw a grid on the screen. 3. Repeatedly asks the user to enter the radius of a circle and a point x,y. Call the draw_circle(pen, radius, x, y) function to draw the circle.

Set your turtle speed to 0 as this may take a while to be drawn.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 50 0,0 35 100,150 20 -40,-35

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below: Input radius of circle: 50 Input position x,y: 0,0 Input radius of circle: 35 Input position x,y: -100,-150 Input radius of circle: 20 Input position x,y: -40,-35
